paragraphs.source_en: Einstein, Podolsky, and Rosen sought to exploit these relationships to show that each of the particles actually has a definite position and a definite velocity at every given instant of time. Here's how: imagine you mea sure the position of the right-moving particle and in this way learn, indirectly, the position of the left-moving particle. EPR argued that since you have done nothing, absolutely nothing, to the left-moving particle, it must have had this position, and all you have done is determine it, albeit indirectly. They then cleverly pointed out that you could have chosen instead to measure the right-moving particle's velocity. In that case you would have, indirectly, determined the velocity of the left-moving particle without at all disturbing it.
